key_insight: Representation geometry, especially hidden-state dimensionality collapse, appears to control when grokking begins, and can be used to intentionally speed up delayed generalization.
engineering_relevance: Geometric dimensionality regularization offers a practical training-time knob for accelerating generalization in models that otherwise overfit for a long time, including MLPs and transformers.
method: Track hidden representation dimensionality during training
Apply Geometric Dimensionality Regularization (GeomDR) as a spectral regularizer
Adjust intervention schedule and target dimensionality to steer grokking timing
evidence_signal: The abstract reports consistent dimensionality collapse before grokking across modular addition, modular division, and permutation composition tasks, with up to 52× faster grokking versus standard AdamW.
watch_item: The speedup depends on the intervention schedule and chosen target dimensionality, so the regularizer may require careful tuning and may not transfer uniformly across tasks or architectures.
paper_title: How to Tame Grokking: Representation Geometry as a Control Signal
